## Executive Summary

Prism Launcher (v12 line at the pinned commit) is the community's reference-quality open-source
launcher, descended from MultiMC via PolyMC. Its two crown jewels: (1) the **component model** —
an instance is a declarative stack of versioned components (minecraft, loader, mods of the
platform kind) described by mmc-pack.json and resolved against a launcher-owned metadata service
(meta.prismlauncher.org), which insulates the launcher from Mojang format churn and lets bad
upstream metadata be patched server-side without shipping a release; and (2) a complete,
correct Microsoft authentication implementation with both interactive OAuth and device-code
flows, the full Xbox/XSTS error taxonomy, multi-account management, and token refresh.

Everything else is disciplined engineering around those cores: a resumable task graph for
version/asset/library updates, automatic Java runtime discovery AND auto-install from Mojang's
runtime manifests, a unified ResourceAPI over CurseForge/Modrinth/Technic/ATLauncher/FTB/packwiz,
hash-based metadata recovery for unknown local mods, and folder models for every resource type
(mods, resource/texture/shader/data packs, worlds). It is the single richest feature-source for
OmniLauncher; its Qt/C++ implementation does not port to our Tauri stack, but nearly every
behavioral contract does.

## Architecture Components

### Authentication step chain

- **Location**: `launcher/minecraft/auth/`
- **Role**: Complete Microsoft account login, refresh, and ownership verification
- **Sources**: `auth-flow`, `msa-step`, `msa-device`, `xbox-user`, `xsts`, `launcher-login`, `entitlements`, `profile-step`, `account-data`, `account-list`

AuthFlow runs an ordered list of AuthStep objects, each owning one protocol hop: MSAStep
(interactive OAuth authorization-code against login.microsoftonline.com/consumers) or
MSADeviceCodeStep (devicecode + token polling) -> XboxUserStep (user.auth.xboxlive.com) ->
XboxAuthorizationStep (xsts.auth.xboxlive.com, with explicit handling of the XErr taxonomy:
no Xbox account, child account needing family consent, region restrictions — each mapped to a
user-actionable message and help link) -> LauncherLoginStep (api.minecraftservices.com/launcher/
login) -> EntitlementsStep (entitlements/license — ownership proof) -> MinecraftProfileStep
(minecraft/profile — UUID/name) -> GetSkinStep. AccountData serializes the full token state with
expiries for silent refresh; AccountList manages multiple accounts with a default. Never touches
a password — exactly the COMPLIANCE.md §2 contract OmniLauncher must implement.

### Component/meta system

- **Location**: `launcher/minecraft/PackProfile.cpp + launcher/meta/`
- **Role**: Instance = declarative stack of versioned components resolved via a launcher-owned meta service
- **Sources**: `pack-profile`, `component`, `component-update`, `meta-index`, `meta-versionlist`, `cmake`

An instance's mmc-pack.json lists components (e.g. net.minecraft, org.lwjgl3, a mod loader) with
versions. Meta Index/VersionList fetch per-uid version catalogs from meta.prismlauncher.org/v1/
(a service the project generates from Mojang + loader upstreams), and ComponentUpdateTask
resolves the stack — dependency requirements between components, recommended versions, conflict
detection. Because the launcher consumes ITS OWN normalized metadata rather than raw upstream
formats, Mojang/loader format churn and upstream metadata bugs are absorbed server-side. This is
the strongest launcher-architecture idea in the corpus and a direct adopt for Omni (with our own
meta service).

### Instance model

- **Location**: `launcher/InstanceList.cpp + launcher/minecraft/MinecraftInstance.cpp`
- **Role**: Self-contained instance folders with INI settings and per-instance overrides
- **Sources**: `instance-list`, `mc-instance`

An instance is any folder under instances/ containing instance.cfg (INI). InstanceList discovers
and watches them; MinecraftInstance layers per-instance settings (java path/args, memory, window
size, account pinning) over global defaults and materializes the launch profile. Instances are
fully self-contained and copy/export-friendly — a property users rely on heavily and Omni keeps.

### Version/asset update pipeline

- **Location**: `launcher/minecraft/update/ + OneSix/Mojang version formats`
- **Role**: Task graph that makes an instance runnable: version files, libraries, assets, folders
- **Sources**: `onesix`, `mojang-format`, `library`, `rules`, `asset-task`, `libraries-task`

MojangVersionFormat ingests official version JSON; OneSixVersionFormat is the internal superset
(MultiMC lineage) adding patches, jar mods, agents, and overrides. Library models parse gradle
specifiers, evaluate OS/feature rules, and resolve download URLs (with mirror/base overrides);
LibrariesTask and AssetUpdateTask verify-by-hash and download only deltas (assets from
resources.download.minecraft.net per the asset index). LegacyFMLLibrariesTask keeps ancient
Forge versions launchable — deep-history support is part of the product's appeal.

### Launch task chain

- **Location**: `launcher/minecraft/launch/`
- **Role**: Ordered pre-launch steps culminating in JVM assembly and process supervision
- **Sources**: `launch-part`, `auto-java`, `mc-instance`

Launch is itself a task pipeline: ClaimAccount (session locking), AutoInstallJava,
CreateGameFolders, ExtractNatives, EnsureAvailableMemory (checks free RAM before spawning),
EnsureOfflineLibraries, MinecraftTarget (direct-join a server/world on start), then
LauncherPartLaunch assembles the classpath/JVM args and starts the game through the launcher's
Java shim, capturing logs. Clean separation of steps makes failures diagnosable and the chain
extensible — the exact pattern OmniLauncher's Rust core should mirror.

### Java runtime management

- **Location**: `launcher/java/ + launcher/java/download/`
- **Role**: Detect every installed JVM; auto-install the right Mojang runtime when missing
- **Sources**: `java-list`, `java-manifest`, `auto-java`

JavaInstallList sweeps vendor install locations (registry on Windows) and validates candidates
by actually executing a checker; JavaVersion models version/arch compatibility. When an instance
needs a Java it can't find, the java/download tasks fetch Mojang's java-runtime manifest and
install the exact runtime component (ManifestDownloadTask + ArchiveDownloadTask + SymlinkTask),
wired into launch as AutoInstallJava. Users never manually install Java — table stakes for Omni.

### Mod platform integration

- **Location**: `launcher/modplatform/`
- **Role**: One abstraction over CurseForge, Modrinth, Technic, ATLauncher, FTB, packwiz
- **Sources**: `resource-api`, `modplatform-dirs`, `ensure-metadata`

ResourceAPI defines search/version-lookup/download contracts; per-platform clients (flame =
CurseForge, modrinth, technic, atlauncher, ftb/import_ftb/legacy_ftb, packwiz) implement them,
giving the UI a single code path for browsing and installing mods, modpacks, resource packs, and
shaders across platforms. EnsureMetadataTask closes the loop for local files: it hashes unknown
jars and asks the platforms' hash-lookup APIs to recover identity/versions, enabling update
checks on hand-installed mods. Import paths from rival launchers are first-class — a deliberate
migration funnel Omni should copy.

### Resource folder models

- **Location**: `launcher/minecraft/mod/`
- **Role**: Watched, toggleable models for every user-content type
- **Sources**: `resource-model`, `mod-folder`

ResourceFolderModel is a file-watched, Qt-model-backed base for content folders with
enable/disable (file renaming), metadata sidecars, and batch operations; specializations cover
mods, resource packs, texture packs, shader packs, data packs, and world saves. The
generalization beyond 'mods' is what makes the launcher feel complete — Omni inherits the
taxonomy.

## Feature Inventory

### instance-model

| Feature | Maturity | Future-proofing | Omni relevance | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Component-stack instance definition | core | 5/5 | adopt | `pack-profile`, `component-update` |
| Launcher-owned metadata service | core | 5/5 | adapt | `meta-index`, `cmake` |
| Version-file patch system (OneSix) | core | 4/5 | adapt | `onesix` |

**Component-stack instance definition** — Instance = ordered list of versioned components (mmc-pack.json) resolved against a meta index, not a hardcoded 'version + loader' pair.

*Omni notes*: OmniLauncher's instance model should be a component stack from day one — it cleanly hosts OmniLoader, compat layers, and future component kinds.

**Launcher-owned metadata service** — All version metadata is consumed from the project's own normalized service (meta.prismlauncher.org), generated from upstreams; upstream churn and bugs are absorbed server-side.

*Omni notes*: Adopt the pattern; Omni must budget the small meta-service infrastructure (static generation + CDN suffices, per Prism's design).

**Version-file patch system (OneSix)** — Per-instance JSON patches can override/extend any component's version data: custom libraries, jar mods, agents, argument edits.

*Omni notes*: Power-user escape hatch that has kept the MultiMC family alive through every ecosystem shift; Omni should expose the same capability with a friendlier surface.

**Interactive OAuth authorization-code login** — Standards-correct OAuth 2.0 against login.microsoftonline.com/consumers with browser handoff.

**Device-code login fallback** — Full devicecode+polling implementation for environments where a browser handoff is awkward.

*Omni notes*: Also the right dev-mode flow for Omni before our Azure client ID is approved (COMPLIANCE.md §2).

**XSTS error taxonomy handling** — Every known XErr (no Xbox profile, child account, region block) maps to a specific user-actionable message with help links.

*Omni notes*: Auth failure UX is where launchers lose users; this taxonomy is ready-made requirements text for Omni.

**Multi-account management with silent refresh** — Multiple Microsoft accounts, default selection, serialized token state with expiries, background refresh, per-instance account pinning.

**Automatic Java runtime install** — Fetches Mojang java-runtime manifests and installs the exact required runtime at launch time when missing.

## Authentication Flows

### Microsoft account login (interactive and device-code)

The complete EULA-compliant Java Edition login chain as implemented by AuthFlow's step list.
Prism uses the api.minecraftservices.com/launcher/login and /entitlements/license endpoints (the
official-launcher-style pair). No password ever transits the launcher; consent happens in
Microsoft's surfaces. Token state (MSA access+refresh, XBL, XSTS, Minecraft token, expiries) is
serialized per account for silent refresh.

Steps:

1. MSAStep (interactive: …/consumers/oauth2/v2.0/authorize + token) or MSADeviceCodeStep (…/devicecode + token polling) -> Microsoft access + refresh tokens
2. XboxUserStep: POST user.auth.xboxlive.com/user/authenticate -> XBL token + user hash
3. XboxAuthorizationStep: POST xsts.auth.xboxlive.com/xsts/authorize -> XSTS token (XErr taxonomy handled: no profile / child / region)
4. LauncherLoginStep: POST api.minecraftservices.com/launcher/login -> Minecraft access token
5. EntitlementsStep: GET api.minecraftservices.com/entitlements/license -> ownership proof
6. MinecraftProfileStep: GET api.minecraftservices.com/minecraft/profile -> UUID + username
7. GetSkinStep: fetch active skin for UI

*Sources*: `auth-flow`, `msa-step`, `msa-device`, `xbox-user`, `xsts`, `launcher-login`, `entitlements`, `profile-step`, `wiki-msauth`

## File Formats

### instance.cfg (ini)

- **Path pattern**: `instances/<name>/instance.cfg`
- **Sources**: `instance-list`, `mc-instance`

INI marker+settings file that makes a folder an instance: name, icon, notes, and per-instance
overrides (java path/args, memory, window geometry, account, wrapper commands). Anything unset
falls through to global settings — a two-layer settings model Omni should keep.

### mmc-pack.json (json)

- **Path pattern**: `instances/<name>/mmc-pack.json`
- **Sources**: `pack-profile`, `component`

The component stack: formatVersion plus an ordered 'components' list of {uid, version,
important/dependencyOnly flags, cached requires}. The de-facto interchange format of the
MultiMC family — Omni's importer must read it, and Omni's native instance format should be a
superset.

### OneSix version file (json)

- **Path pattern**: `instances/<name>/patches/<uid>.json + meta cache`
- **Sources**: `onesix`

Internal version-data format (superset of Mojang's): mainClass, +libraries/+jarMods/+agents
additions, argument edits, traits. Both the meta service's payload format and the per-instance
patch override format.

### Mojang version manifest + asset index (json)

- **Path pattern**: `meta upstream / assets/indexes/<id>.json`
- **Sources**: `mojang-format`, `asset-task`

Official upstream formats (version JSON: libraries with rules/natives/downloads, arguments,
assetIndex; asset index: name -> {hash, size} objects fetched from
resources.download.minecraft.net/<h2>/<hash>). Prism ingests them into the internal model —
Omni will consume the same upstreams through its own meta layer.

## Protocols & API Surfaces

### Microsoft/Xbox/Minecraft auth chain

- **Endpoint**: `login.microsoftonline.com/consumers, user.auth.xboxlive.com, xsts.auth.xboxlive.com, api.minecraftservices.com`
- **Sources**: `msa-step`, `msa-device`, `xbox-user`, `xsts`, `launcher-login`, `entitlements`, `profile-step`

Exact endpoints verified in source: /consumers/oauth2/v2.0/{authorize,token,devicecode};
user.auth.xboxlive.com/user/authenticate; xsts.auth.xboxlive.com/xsts/authorize;
api.minecraftservices.com/{launcher/login, entitlements/license, minecraft/profile}. This is
COMPLIANCE.md §2 made concrete.

### Launcher meta service

- **Endpoint**: `https://meta.prismlauncher.org/v1/`
- **Sources**: `meta-index`, `cmake`

Static JSON index: a root index of component uids, per-uid version lists, per-version OneSix
payloads. CDN-friendly, cacheable, offline-tolerant. The build URL is a CMake cache variable —
forks point it at their own service, which is exactly what Omni will do.

### Mojang download CDNs

- **Endpoint**: `resources.download.minecraft.net, libraries.minecraft.net (via version JSON URLs)`
- **Sources**: `asset-task`, `libraries-task`, `buildconfig`

Assets by content hash under resources.download.minecraft.net/<h2>/<hash>; libraries from the
URLs the version JSON declares. Hash-verified, delta-only downloads.

## Analysis Notes

### What Omni adopts wholesale vs re-architects

Adopt behaviorally: component-stack instances, launcher-owned meta, the full auth chain +
error taxonomy, auto-Java, unified ResourceAPI, hash metadata recovery, migration importers,
pre-launch task pipeline. Re-architect: all of it lands in Rust/Tauri instead of Qt/C++ —
Prism's Qt model/view coupling is its biggest source of complexity and does not port. Behavioral
contracts (formats, endpoints, step ordering, error cases) are stack-independent and now
captured in this analysis.

*Sources*: `resource-api`, `pack-profile`, `auth-flow`

### Offline-play handling is compliance-sensitive

Prism supports offline sessions (EnsureOfflineLibraries exists to keep launch working without
network). Omni policy per COMPLIANCE.md: offline convenience for verified owners is acceptable;
anything enabling play without ownership verification is not. Phase 3 must specify Omni's
offline semantics precisely (cached entitlement + expiry window) rather than inheriting behavior
implicitly.

*Sources*: `launch-part`, `entitlements`

### Version/tooling facts at pin

Launcher_VERSION_MAJOR = 12 (CMakeLists.txt); Qt 6 / C++; meta URL and resource base are build
-time configurable (Launcher_META_URL cache var, DEFAULT_RESOURCE_BASE in BuildConfig.h);
GPL-3.0-only license (COPYING.md) with MultiMC-heritage files — license terms recorded for
ADR-0002 fact-use only; no Prism code is copied into Omni products.

*Sources*: `cmake`, `buildconfig`
